tools.name: stripe (npm package)
tools.detail: Backend generates a Checkout Session and returns the checkout URL

claims: Stripe documentation makes the integration smooth
Flow: plans page fetches plans from backend; each plan has a Stripe ID; frontend posts the ID; backend creates a session with the stripe npm package and returns the checkout URL; frontend redirects
how_to_steps: Store a Stripe price ID on each plan record in the backend
Plans page fetches plans from the backend and shows them
On plan select, frontend sends the Stripe ID to the backend
Backend creates a Checkout Session via the stripe npm package and returns the checkout URL
Frontend redirects the user to the Stripe-hosted checkout
Build success and cancel return pages
Then implement Stripe webhooks to receive payment events in real time
on_screen_only: Dark room, dual monitors with a code editor (unreadable code), captions of spoken words (e.g. 'INTEGRATING STRIPE FOR', 'A CORRESPONDING STRIPE', 'TO THE BACKEND.', 'USER GETS REDIRECTED', 'REAL TIME')
No repo, framework or product name visible

relevance.why: Standard Stripe Checkout pattern that Claude Code produces from the docs in one pass; nothing a veteran builder does not know. The webhook step is the only part that matters and is not shown yet.

implement_score.why: Already the default Stripe approach; the one reminder worth applying is to treat webhooks (not the success page) as the source of truth for entitlement.

verify: Which framework/backend he uses (not shown) and whether later days cover webhook signature verification and idempotency

gap.what: Generic Stripe Checkout how-to; no AI angle and no new tool. Not covered in liked set but not a gap worth filling.
